sentences.text: Bilophila wadsworthia is an obligately anaerobic, sulfite-reducing, Gram-negative bacterium described as a common human pathobiont inhabiting the distal intestinal tract.
It is reported to use a diverse range of food- and host-derived sulfonates to generate sulfite as a terminal electron acceptor for anaerobic respiration, converting sulfonate sulfur to H2S.

A study reported that it colonises the gut of germ-free male mice fed a high-fat diet using microcompartment and anaerobic energy genes, metabolising taurine and isethionate to H2S, acetate and ethanol.
High-fat diets have been reported to reshape gut microbiota composition and promote expansion of this sulfidogenic bacterium, which has been linked to inflammation and gut barrier dysfunction.
Published work describes it as often isolated from patients diagnosed with appendicitis and inflammatory bowel disease, with the H2S it forms implicated in inflammatory conditions and colon cancer.
